content:
In an effort to try and make it easier for people working on Physlib to get credit for tasks for which it has traditionally been hard to get credit for in academia, but which are important to this changing world, I've made:

https://contributions.physlib.io

The idea is that people submit reports based on their work in one of six areas: Review, Maintenance, Refactoring, Foundation work, Formalisation, and Documentation. With their report they provide evidence of their work, which is checked by a maintainer. Once checked their report is digitally signed, and converted into a verifiable certificate using the Open Badge 3.0 protocol. This report can then be cited, put on a CV etc. The certificate can also be verified as valid by any independent party supporting the Open Badge 3.0 protocol.

One way to view this is: like an arXiv for human contributions.

The code for the site is here: https://github.com/jstoobysmith/PhyslibContributors, and everything works through GitHub (which implies no server costs, and the only account people need is a GitHub account).

In the future, if there is interest, the scope of this could be increased to also cover Mathlib and CSLib. However for now it is just restricted to Physlib.

Happy to hear any feedback. It is very much still in 'beta' phase.

Many thanks to @Nathaneal Sajan for helping with parts of this. The site was initially vibe-coded, but everything has been carefully checked.
